shortDescription: Supporting successful curriculum reform and strengthening learning outcomes
description: Sri Lanka begins rolling out its new curriculum in Grades 1 and 6 in 2026, alongside a national learning assessment. This reform has the potential to modernise teaching and restore learning trajectories after years of disruption, but challenges remain. One key challenge is not the design of the curriculum but its acceptance—by teachers accustomed to tuition-driven, exam-focused practices, and by communities that may be wary of pedagogical change. The priority for 2026 is to ensure the reform succeeds by helping identify bottlenecks early, monitoring classroom realities, and supporting strategies that build teacher and community confidence in the new approach. As details of implementation become clearer in Q1, UNICEF will refine the support package, with particular attention to child-centered pedagogy and development of a teacher professional development framework, strengthening monitoring and mentoring mechanisms, education behaviour change, communication, and practical tools that help teachers make the shift in pedagogy but support to ensure a successful reform journey for Sri Lanka is required.
objectives:
Early implementation bottleneck and classroom reality brief. Rapid analysis of on-the-ground implementation challenges during the 2026 rollout, drawing on classroom observation, teacher feedback, and assessment signals.

Targeted behaviour-change and communication support package. A focused set of practical tools and messaging to build teacher and community confidence in the new curriculum and support shifts in pedagogy.

Development of national learning assessment system. Supporting the MoE to design and develop a national assessment system for primary school learning outcomes and capacity strengthening for use of data.

shortDescription: The strategic purpose of this request is to lay the foundation for integrated VAC prevention and response programme management
description: The strategic purpose of this request is to lay the foundation for integrated VAC prevention and response programme management. Addressing VAC in BiH requires moving beyond fragmented, sectoral, project-based interventions. Thus support is needed to establish programme management structure within the CO with identifying entry points, including catalytic policy and financing. The goal is to shift from siloed interventions to integrated, system-wide programming. UNICEF BiH seeks support in designing and operationalizing VAC related interventions, including programme design for high impact violence prevention solutions. CoE support is requested to conduct a scoping analysis of VAC policy environment, coordination structures, and delivery mechanisms. The TA would guide the design of a cross sectoral operational framework, define roles, propose budget lines and financing options, and develop a monitoring and learning agenda. Special attention should be given to integrating VAC work with the implementation of the European Child Guarantee, de-institutionalization reform, educational, and juvenile justice programmes. This technical support will be very timely also in light of the planned recruitment of a Child Protection Specialist in January 2026 in laying the groundwork for a more cohesive and strategic VAC portfolio, addressing current fragmentation and enabling UNICEF to engage holistically in this critical area

shortDescription: Provide guidance on successful EdTech tools and programmes to improve foundational learning, with focus on the use of EdTech to assist teachers in conducting fo
description:
UNICEF Indonesia office has recently kicked off a partnership with Gates Foundation and Tanoto Foundation on a programme to improve foundational learning (FAASTER programme).



As part of this programme, we have an EdTech component where we plan to use an app to assist teachers in conducting formative assessment and using student learning data to better inform classroom instructions. The goal is to strengthen individualized/remedial support for low-performing students through effective use of learning data.



We are currently in the inception phase and consulting relevant stakeholders to inform our programme design. We would greatly appreciate the opportunity to connect with your team to learn about successful EdTech programmes in other UNICEF country contexts, key lessons learned, and considerations for implementation.


In particular, we are interested in EIDU’s work in Kenya, which supports teachers in using technology for lesson planning and assessment; our programme is also centered around structured pedagogy as is the EIDU platform. We would appreciate if we can also discuss potential ways to connect with EIDU, as I understand they are part of the Blue Unicorn portfolio
objectives: Successful selection of EdTech partner/tool to support UNICEF CO to implement the FAASTER programme.

All the best,
Aspa

shortDescription: The technical assistance aims to support El Salvador in developing a comprehensive, nation-wide strategy for adolescents that promotes a coordinated,
description: The technical assistance aims to support El Salvador in developing a comprehensive, nation-wide strategy for adolescents that promotes a coordinated, system-level approach to their wellbeing, protection, and opportunities. This support will help national institutions generate and use evidence on adolescents’ needs, harmonize fragmented initiatives, and define clear priorities across sectors such as education, health, protection, skills, and participation. By facilitating inter-institutional dialogue, strengthening analytical and planning capacities, and promoting alignment with national policies, the assistance seeks to establish a coherent framework that guides investments and programmes for adolescents, ensuring more equitable, effective, and sustainable outcomes at scale.
objectives:
National adolescent strategy drafted and validated with government institutions and key stakeholders.

Prioritized multisector framework outlining goals, interventions, and indicators for adolescent wellbeing.

Clear implementation roadmap with roles, coordination mechanisms, and timelines.

Strengthened national capacity to plan, coordinate, and monitor adolescent-related policies and programmes.

shortDescription: The technical assistance aims to support El Salvador in strategically integrating artificial intelligence (AI) across the education system to enhance
description: The technical assistance aims to support El Salvador in strategically integrating artificial intelligence (AI) across the education system to enhance learning outcomes, equity, and teacher quality. UNICEF will provide expertise in designing AI-powered tools for personalized student learning, virtual tutoring, and real-time progress monitoring, as well as innovative teacher training programs with feedback and coaching. The support includes developing data-driven decision-making platforms, adapting international best practices, and ensuring inclusive approaches for vulnerable populations. Ultimately, this technical assistance will help operationalize AI solutions, strengthen national capacity, and accelerate the country’s path toward globally competitive education outcomes and sustainable system-level transformation
objectives:
AI-powered teacher training modules implemented for continuous professional development.

Personalized student learning platforms deployed with adaptive content and virtual tutors.

Real-time education data system operational for monitoring learning outcomes and informing policy.

Targeted support programs for vulnerable students established to reduce learning gaps.

Capacity-building framework for national stakeholders to sustain and scale AI-driven educational innovations.

shortDescription: 【UTS】Assess septic tanks’ impact on groundwater quality (safely managed sanitation) in Kiritimati

objectives: Generate practical evidence on whether septic systems are affecting groundwater quality in a vulnerable island hydrogeology context, strengthening decision-making for safely managed sanitation. shortDescription: Scale justice for children from pilot initiatives to a national system
description: UNICEF is currently implementing an integrated service package for justice for children in one major urban area (Kandy). By end-Q1 2026, the first six months of implementation of this pilot will provide operational evidence to assess functionality, gaps, and system-readiness for expansion. UNICEF will need to assess and use that evidence to propose a cost-efficient pathway for sustainable scale-up nationwide. This will likely include adjusting institutional responsibilities, refining the model based on early lessons, and developing a scalable financing and workforce approach. The specifics—appropriate sequencing, cost implications, and political feasibility—will become clearer once early performance data and feedback is analysed with UNICEF’s aim being to ensure that a realistic, evidence-based scale-up plan is on the table for government consideration by Q2/Q3 to feed into the preparation of the 2027 budget planning process.
objectives:
Pilot performance and system-readiness assessment. An evidence-based assessment of the first six months of implementation, identifying what works, what needs adjustment, and the system implications for scale-up.
Costed national scale-up pathway for justice for children. A phased, financially and institutionally feasible plan for national expansion, designed to feed directly into 2027 budget and policy processes

description: We are asking for support for conducting EPR simulation for 2,5 days, meaning that some 4-7 days are needed (depending on travel arrangements and Visa procedures including travel time). objectives:
Subject: Request for Giulia Gagliardini's support - MENARO Facilitation team Emergency Preparedness Simulation Exercise Tunisia/Libya 15-19 June 2026

I am reaching out to kindly request Giulia’s support to participate to the joint Emergency Preparedness and Response Simulation exercise with Tunisia and Libya Country Offices the week of 15-19 June 2026.  

 Giulia has been key in developing the concept for the simulation and been Emergency Focal Point Tunisia in the RO, and she will additionally also bring a comprehensive UNICEF perspective, based on her extensive field-, RO- and programme perspective and capacities, including emergency preparedness, response and coordination experience. Having her in the facilitation team would bring much added value to the simulation and a true asset for the work of improving Tunisia’s preparedness. She would also be able to build on recent work in the region with Preparedness across countries, including contingency planning for “children on the move”.

We will conduct this simulation as part of UNICEF Emergency Preparedness commitments. Please find attached draft concept note.

The facilitator role includes:

Before simulation – Preparations (4-5 hours)

  • Participating in introductory sessions with the consultant
  • Pre-reading of simulation materials

During simulation - In country (3,5 days)

  • Detailed planning in country 0,5-1 day
  • Supporting introduction to emergency preparedness and response concepts 0,5 days
  • Facilitation of joint simulation – 2 days
    • Guiding the COs through an emergency scenario
    • Launching simulation learning injects and ensure steering vis-à-vis learning objectives, provide guiding relevant emergency preparedness and response advise/steer.
    • Observation and monitoring, and measure against simulation deliverables
    • Supporting debrief, and guiding the CO in drawing lessons learned and action points.

After simulation

  • Contribute to observations and key findings for the final report, produced by the consultant (1 hour)

The estimate costs for DSA and Travel (Lib 1800-2000 USD/person for one week, Tun 1900-2100 USD/person for one week). DSA and Travel costs will be borne by MENARO Humanitarian Team unless otherwise agreed upon. Focal point in our team is Per Velandia.

In order to swiftly initiate lengthy Visa procedures, (or search for other options) we would kindly as for a reply as soon as possible.

 

Thank you very much for your kind consideration.

Kind regards, Segolene

shortDescription: Selection of Food Technologist to Support Pillar 1 of Tanzania's FFA
description:
Support the selection process of the following individual consultancy process:

Food Technologist (Complementary Foods) – National Individual Consultant

Scope of Work:

The purpose of this consultancy is to support the development, validation, and scale-up of affordable, safe, and nutrient-dense complementary food products for children aged 6–23 months in Tanzania. 

Key Tasks

• Conduct landscape analysis and stakeholder engagement by reviewing existing complementary food products, supply chains, and regulatory frameworks, mapping key actors (e.g. manufacturers, laboratories, ingredient suppliers, distributors, government agencies, NGOs and academia institutions), and defining product profiles in consultation with stakeholders. With special focus in prioritized regions: Dar es Salaam, Arusha, Mbeya, Mwanza and Zanzibar.
• Support the validation of the mapping report and database creation of local food producers. 
• Support with key partners product research, development, and validation by formulating and optimizing at least two nutrient-dense complementary food products using locally available ingredients. This includes ensuring adequate nutrient density, protein quality, micronutrient bioavailability (e.g. iron, zinc) energy density, safety, and sensory acceptability; defining processing and packaging parameters (e.g. extrusion, roasting, germination), packaging specifications and critical control points; and overseeing laboratory testing and refinement through accredited labs and refine formulations accordingly. 
• Strengthen food safety, quality assurance, and regulatory compliance systems by supporting the development and implementation of training toolkits (including HACCP, GMP, and SSOP protocols); support building capacity of producers and quality assurance teams through targeted training; developing compliant product labeling in line with national regulations and the International Code of Marketing of Breast-milk Substitutes; and establishing shelf-life testing protocols as well as market surveillance and monitoring mechanisms.
• Support local producers and SMEs through continuous, hands-on technical assistance to improve production processes of nutritious first foods, ensure food safety and quality standards are met, and facilitate reformulation of existing products to meet national and international standards.
• In collaboration with key partners support the development of business and distribution models by designing costed, sustainable approaches for production and last-mile delivery; identifying risks and mitigation strategies; and exploring market feasibility of the developed products, based on evidence generated.
• Support the development of technical tools and strengthen capacity among governments, producers, SMEs, and partners through training materials, standard operating procedures (SOPs), workshops, webinars, and on-site coaching, promoting long-term sustainability using the training toolkit developed by UNICEF.
• Facilitate knowledge sharing and coordination by establishing and maintaining a network of local farmers, processors, and stakeholders to promote quality assurance, innovation, and continuous learning, while ensuring regular coordination with UNICEF and partners. 
• Support the generation and dissemination of evidence on product acceptability, shelf-life, and market potential, and compile a final report summarizing key findings, achievements, challenges, and recommendations for scale-up.
• Support other activities agreed as relevant to the objectives of the consultancy.

It will also reinforce national nutrition strategies and innovative financing, leveraging mechanisms such as the Child Nutrition Fund to ensure sustainable interventions across health, food, education, and social protection systems.
objectives:
Policy and Governance 

Legislative proposals developed for maternal and child nutrition governance reforms. 

Drafted and validated nutrition policy implementation roadmap. 

Knowledge Generation 

National knowledge-generation agenda aligned with Niger’s priorities completed. 

Repository of evidence-based practices and research gaps established. 

Financing and Sustainability 

Innovative financing models documented, including Child Nutrition Fund operational plan. 

Resource mobilization strategy for scalable interventions across systems finalized. 

Capacity Strengthening 

Nutrition team trained in governance, financing, and accountability mechanisms
